text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#INC-4998 - GPU memory pressure on pool infer-east-1a. Trigger: sustained GPU mem > 88% for 2m. Grafana: https://grafana.example/d/gpu-pools
pagerduty: INC-4998 auto-assigned to aj (oncall), escalation to dan in 8m if unacked.
aj: acked, oncall here. seeing repeated 'CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY' + 'cuMemAlloc' traces in container logs. tagging @maya for SRE assistance.
maya: ack. initial triage: kvcache size increasing rapidly on pod sessions owned by large-tenant 'alpha-inc'. evictions spike then kernel allocation failures. CPU fine. Starting traffic steering to infer-east-1c and adjust batch caps.
cleo: logs: ```[2026-03-14T22:05:21Z] runtime[worker-21]: cuda cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory, requested 1.5GB
[2026-03-14T22:05:22Z] kvcache: shard-04 usage=4.2GB evictions=2400``` Also noticed one GPU showing ECC corrected errors; could indicate previous fragmentation.
ryan: support: customers reporting timeouts on /v1/chat and /v1/generate. Two customers filing support tickets. Status page draft at https://status.redwood.example/INC-4998. Recommend 'degraded' state.
incident-bot: status page update queued: 'degraded' for routes [/v1/chat,/v1/generate] in us-east.
maya: mitigation plan -> 1) lower batch size for top-3 heavy routes; 2) add fallback to rwd-8b-quant at 50%; 3) cordon + drain 2 problematic nodes; 4) restart runtime on drained nodes; 5) schedule follow-up for kvcache cap. Executing step 1 & 2 now.
aj: running: ```redwood route update --route /v1/generate --overrides '{"max_batch_size":3}'``` and ```redwood rollout set-fallback --route /v1/generate --fallback-model rwd-8b-quant --percent 50```
(terminal): `OK updated, fallback started`
cleo: traffic shift observable: 47% of sessions now routed to fallback model. Latencies drop from ~6s to ~1.2s for fallback users. Some legacy sessions pinned to node-22 still failing.
dan: escalated in PD and joining. what's node state?
aj: node-22 has repeated kernel OOM logs, 2 pods in CrashLoopBackOff due to cuMemAlloc. drain stuck because pods are pinned (long sessions). options: force-evict or reboot GPU. leaning to force-evict then restart runtime.
maya: agree force-evict. run force delete plus restart runtime container. Cleo can you capture the pre-restart logs for postmortem?
cleo: capturing logs now. snippet saved to s3: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/INC-4998/node-22-pre-restart.log
aj: executing: `kubectl delete pod session-22-7a3 --namespace inference --grace-period=0 --force` -> returned `pod deleted`
(terminal): `restarting runtime service on node-22` -> `systemctl restart redwood-runtime` -> `service restarted, GPUs back online`
cleo: after restart, GPU mem stable, no further cuMemAlloc errors on node-22. kvcache evictions normalized.
ryan: support: customer 8421 confirmed degraded cleared for them. I'll update tickets and status page to "partial mitigation".
incident-bot: PagerDuty: INC-4998 acknowledged by aj, escalated to dan, notes updated.
dan: I'll hand back to SRE lead maya after I let things bake 15m. tagging @maya for monitoring handoff.
maya: handing back. continue to watch for re-occurrence. Postmortem checklist: capture kvcache growth traces, evaluate cap defaults, consider auto-cap on per-tenant heavy shards.
support-bot: Automated: status page updated to 'partial mitigation'. customers notified.
(5m later) aj: no new OOMs in last 10m, metrics trending down. scheduling follow-up incident review. closing PD alert pending postmortem.
(terminal): `pagerduty: Incident INC-4998 status changed to resolved by aj`
